processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 15, 17, 19; this sample x = 19) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h prior to hot rolling.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm; plates were then cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining.
Parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq; the solution-treated state is the baseline for subsequent aging.
Solution-treated 19Al samples aged at 525 °C for 6 h, followed by water quenching; this is the terminal state defining this sample.

structures.overall_structure: Predominantly α (BCC) matrix with only a small amount of β-Mn precipitated. In the 19Al (highest-Al) alloy, aging at 525 °C produces very slow β-Mn precipitation kinetics, so the α matrix remains largely untransformed and the hardness increase is minimal.

phases_present.morphology: matrix (largely untransformed at this low-temperature aging condition)
thin network along α grain boundaries plus a small amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn within α grains

precipitates.distribution: along α grain boundaries and a small amount within α grains
fine particles dispersed in the α matrix

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers indentation with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of solution-treated and aged Fe-Mn-Al-Cu samples (identify the aging hardening behavior)
characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al aged at 525 °C for 6 h = 594.9 ± 5.7 HV; the 525 °C series of the 19Al alloy stays lowest (~590–620 HV) among the aging temperatures

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al aged at 525 °C (incl. 6 h): α matrix largely retained, with only a small amount of β-Mn decorating α grain boundaries and short rod-shaped β-Mn inside grains; α-Mn particles also present

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm (low magnification) and 0.05 μm (high magnification)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases and their distribution after aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu steels are single-phase α (BCC); in the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C the α matrix is retained with a thin β-Mn network along grain boundaries

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EDS detector on ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM (and TEM EDS)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure chemical compositions of the alloys (Table 1) and of phases
characterization_methods.key_findings: EDS-measured composition of the 19Al alloy: Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (at.%)

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases of the alloys after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: After the selected aging treatments the alloys contain α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn, indicating that α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before the α matrix fully transformed to β-Mn (note: XRD was run on the 19Al 550 °C/6 h condition, not on this 525 °C/6 h sample)

unmapped_findings: 19Al alloy chemical composition (EDS, Table 1): Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (at.%).
The solution-treated 19Al alloy (common baseline for all 19Al aging conditions, before this sample's 525 °C/6 h aging) had a Vickers hardness of 263.8 ± 1.1 HV.
The 19Al alloy density measured by the Archimedes method is 6.66 g·cm⁻³.

For the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C, only a small amount of β-Mn precipitated even after 10 h (12.1 %), giving a minimal hardness increase; at 525 °C the β-Mn precipitation is the slowest of the three Al contents, illustrating that increasing Al content slows the β-Mn precipitation kinetics during aging.
The highest Vickers hardness of the 19Al alloy (917.8 HV) was reached at 600 °C for 10 h, not at the 525 °C/6 h condition of this sample.

The elastic modulus used in the indentation fracture-toughness equation is 181 GPa for the 19Al alloy (from compressive stress-strain curves); this value belongs to the hardest 19Al sample, not to this 525 °C/6 h condition.
Vickers-indenter cracks generated in the ultra-hard 19Al sample had an average crack length of 35 μm, and its KIC was 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 (measured on the hardest sample, not on this 525 °C/6 h condition).
